Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror movies that cover a range of sub‑genres—from supernatural chills to psychological dread:

| # | Title | Year | Sub‑genre | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|-----------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **Psycho** | 1960 | Psychological / Thriller | Hitchcock’s masterclass in suspense; the shower scene is legendary. |
| 2 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Psychological / Supernatural | Kubrick’s eerie adaptation of Stephen King’s novel; haunting visuals and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 3 | **Halloween** | 1978 | Slasher | John Carpenter’s film that defined the slasher genre; Michael Myers’ silent menace remains iconic. |
| 4 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | Supernatural | One of the most terrifying exorcism stories ever told; its impact on horror cinema is immeasurable. |
| 5 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Psychological / Supernatural | A modern masterpiece that blends family drama with creeping dread; Toni Collette delivers a career‑shaping performance. |
| 6 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Horror / Social Commentary | Jordan Peele’s sharp satire wrapped in a tense thriller; it won an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay. |
| 7 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Survival / Sci‑Fi | Silence is the key weapon here; the tension is palpable throughout. |
| 8 | **It Follows** | 2014 | Supernatural / Psychological | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” trope; the soundtrack adds to the unsettling atmosphere. |
| 9 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Folk Horror | A daylight horror that turns the sunny Swedish setting into a nightmare; the ritual scenes are unforgettable. |
|10 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Psychological / Supernatural | A metaphorical look at grief that becomes genuinely scary; the creature design is both creepy and symbolic. |
|11 | **The Ring** | 2002 | Supernatural / Mystery | An American remake of a Japanese film that still feels fresh; the cursed videotape concept is chilling. |
|12 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Found Footage / Supernatural | Low‑budget but effective; the jump scares feel real because they’re presented as “home video.” |
|13 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | Meta‑Horror | A clever twist on the cabin‑in‑the‑woods trope; it deconstructs horror clichés while delivering genuine scares. |
|14 | **Suspiria** | 1977 | Supernatural / Gothic | Dario Argento’s visually stunning film; the color palette and score create a dreamlike terror. |
|15 | **The Witch** | 2015 | Historical / Supernatural | A slow‑burn horror set in 1630s New England; the period detail and atmospheric dread make it unforgettable. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred style—whether you like a psychological mind‑bender, a supernatural ghost story, or a slasher flick. Happy watching!
